newsitem.title: UK: UK traders put hefty bets on Labour election win.
newsitem.headline: UK traders put hefty bets on Labour election win.

text.p: Traders in the traditionally Conservative-backing City of London heaped money on the opposition Labour Party in frenzied last-minute gambling on the eve of Britain's election.

Labour's predicted majority hit record highs at the financial bookmakers on Wednesday as City traders placed hefty bets ahead of the May 1 vote, which opinion polls suggest will deliver a resounding victory for the opposition.
"(The majority) is the highest it's been. It's extremely busy," said Martin Slaney, financial dealer at City Index.

City Index quoted Labour's anticipated majority at 108-118 -- its highest since the election campaign began six weeks ago -- meaning a punter who expected the winning margin to top that could buy at 118.
Slaney said stakes of around 500 pounds ($814) per seat had become commonplace. "There's huge size in everything," he said.
Patrick Jay, head of the sports desk -- which covers political betting -- at IG Index, quoted a majority of 105-115, with Labour forecast to win 382-388 seats to the Conservatives' 215-221.
"It's gone absolutely insane," he said. "The sky's the limit."

Two opinion polls published on Wednesday gave Labour 18 and 20 percentage-point leads over the Conservatives. A 20-point advantage would translate into a majority of more than 200 seats in Britain's 659-seat parliament.
Reuters' final survey of 20 top political experts predicted a smaller Labour majority of 92.
-- Abigail Levene, London Newsroom +44-171-542-8968 ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
